title: GPA sync writes millisecond timestamps into freshness state that is compared in seconds

evidence.quote:

await upsertSyncState(db, {

  last_sync: Date.now(),

reasoning: freshness.ts receives nowSeconds and compares last_sync against second-based thresholds, and the freshness tests construct last_sync in seconds. resumeGpaSync persists Date.now(), which is milliseconds. That makes nowSeconds - last_sync a large negative number, so a GPA sync written by gpa-sync can appear fresh long after it should be stale.
reproduction: After resumeGpaSync writes last_sync around 1780360000000, buildFreshnessSummary with nowSeconds around 1780360000 computes a negative age and does not mark gpa stale even after the 7-day threshold.
recommendation: Persist GPA sync_state timestamps in seconds with Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) or unixepoch(), consistently with other sync writers. Consider normalizing existing millisecond last_sync rows during deploy if values exceed a seconds-range threshold.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included freshness tests validate second-based inputs, but no included test connects resumeGpaSync's persisted sync_state value to buildFreshnessSummary.
suggestedRegressionTest: Mock upsertSyncState in resumeGpaSync and assert last_sync is a Unix-seconds value; add an integration-style freshness test using the written value after advancing nowSeconds beyond gpaMaxAgeSeconds.
minimumFixScope: apps/api/src/services/gpa-sync.ts, with optional data cleanup for existing sync_state rows.
